text: Step 1 — Read tidy IBTrACS file (read_ibtracs_clean()). Standardise column names, keep wind pressure fields, convert wind-radii units km, restrict Atlantic basin. Step 2 — Keep nearby track points. every six-hour position record, measure great-circle distance site discard points beyond search_radius_km. Step 3 — Estimate wind site (compute_site_winds_full()). Work side storm site sits , look directional wind radii, estimate eye radius (estimate_RMW_knaff()), evaluate Holland wind-profile formula — small adjustment fast storm moving. output estimated wind site_wind_kt every track point. Step 4 — Group track points events (make_storm_events()). Combine 6-hourly points one summary row per (storm, site), peak site wind, mean eye radius, timing, pressure. event labelled TS (34–63 kt) HUR (≥ 64 kt). Step 5 — Measure often storms hit (compute_annual_counts() → compute_lambda_table()). Turn per-year counts average rates (lambda) measure clustered busy quiet seasons (k_hat). Step 6 — Roll synthetic seasons (simulate_twolevel_counts()). synthetic year: first draw activity multiplier (quiet hyperactive season?), total storm count consistent , finally split total tropical storms hurricanes. "cosine" draws smooth bell curve wind event; "uniform" gives every storm day wind — useful sensitivity tests. background_wind. code: library(ipdcstorm)  targets <- tibble::tribble(   ~name,       ~lat,     ~lon,   "St_Martin", 18.0708, -63.0501,   "Saba",      17.6350, -63.2300,   "Statia",    17.4890, -62.9740 )  cfg <- make_hazard_cfg(   data_path        = system.file("extdata", "ibtracs_demo.csv",                                  package = "ipdcstorm"),   simulation_years = 1000,   climate          = make_climate_cfg(scenario = "stationary") )  out <- run_hazard_model(cfg, targets = targets, seed = 42)  daily <- generate_daily_hazard_impact_spatial(   out         = out,   location    = targets$name,   sim_years   = seq_len(1000),   year0       = 2000L,   damage      = list(method = "intensity"),   pulse_shape = "cosine",   scenario    = "baseline",   seed        = 42 )

Direct mode: provide delta_sst explicitly. delta_sst resolved, downstream hazard logic depends resolved delta_sst fixed model settings. Scenario names timing retained provenance metadata. direct delta_sst scenario-derived inputs supplied, must resolve delta_sst error raised. scenario = "stationary" delta_sst supplied, returned config represents canonical baseline hazard-model specification delta_sst = 0. what: Run the three-tier hazard model validation suite — run_validation_suite
title: Run the three-tier hazard model validation suite — run_validation_suite
text: Evaluates stationary climate-adjusted hazard model historical record using three complementary checks: Tier 1 — Hindcast (return levels) Withholds recent holdout_years record, re-fits model training period, simulates n_sim synthetic years, compares GEV-based return levels estimated full observed record. location/return-period pair passes (\(\checkmark\)) simulated return level falls within observed conf_level confidence interval. Tier 2 — Storm rate check Compares calibrated annual TS hurricane passage rates per location published HURDAT2/IBTrACS reference bounds. Rates outside reference range flagged may indicate search-radius record-length issue. Tier 3 — Wind field spot-checks Compares Holland wind-profile site estimates historical station observations individual storm passages. comparison graded observation-quality-dependent tolerance band (: \(\pm\)15%, B: \(\pm\)25%, C: \(\pm\)35%). Results printed console , cfg$save_plots cfg$save_tables TRUE, written cfg$out_dir.

title: Select k representative stress-test years with good sample coverage — select_stress_years
text: Picks small subset k years candidate set collectively represent full distribution stress severity.  Three selection strategies available: "stratified" (default) Divides composite_score range k equal-count bins returns year whose score closest bin's median.  Guarantees one representative per severity level — near-miss worst-case. "diverse" Greedy maximin selection normalised metric space.  Starts extreme year, iteratively adds year furthest already-selected years.  Maximises spread multi-dimensional metric space. "top" Returns k years highest composite_score.  Useful goal set purely high-severity scenarios. Portfolio mode vs per-location mode: metrics location column (typical output aggregate_stress_metrics() multiple locations), rows treated single pool k years selected full portfolio.  location column present (single-location input pre-aggregated table), selection performed independently within location result sorted location selection_rank. composite_score absent metrics, aggregate_stress_metrics() called internally using supplied weights metrics_used.

title: Simulate annual counts with climate adjustments — simulate_twolevel_counts
text: Non-stationary extension Poisson-Gamma annual count model rate effect intensity effect applied stationary time slice: Rate effect: year's activity factor modulated scalar SST shift: A_t = activity_factor * exp(beta_SST * delta_sst) Intensity effect: storm-class split varies scalar SST shift: p_HUR(t) = clamp(p_HUR_base * (1 + gamma * delta_sst), 0.01, 0.99) N_total_t ~ Poisson(lambda_total * A_t) n_HUR_t ~ Binomial(N_total_t, p_HUR(t)) n_TS_t = N_total_t - n_HUR_t gamma_intensity 0, storm-class split constant. beta_sst gamma_intensity 0, reduces stationary model.

text: End--end convenience wrapper: runs run_hazard_model() run_validation_suite(). recommended entry point standard validation workflows. validation uses three-tier framework: Tier 1 (Hindcast): Hold last N years historical record, simulate synthetic annual maxima training period, compare return levels. simulated return level fall within observed return level's confidence interval (computed via delta-method parametric bootstrap hurdle-GEV model). Tier 2 (Rate check): Compare model storm rates (lambda) published HURDAT2/IBTrACS climatologies target region. Tier 3 (Wind field): Spot-check site-level winds Holland wind profile model historical station observations.
